genre.reader_fantasy: Foreknowledge used decisively; regret repaired; enemies pre-empted before they know there is a fight.

devices.description: Italicized inner line contrasting last time with now (*Last time, I died right here.*). Short; never a paragraph-long recap.
A known future event named with a date or interval; each mention tightens the clock.
A moment where the present visibly departs from the remembered future; must be a canonical event on main and is flagged diverged in the ledger.

register_notes: The regressor often knows more than their rank permits; deference must be rendered as behavior (holding back, deflecting) rather than dropped.
Foreknowledge is never explained aloud unless the contract plans the reveal.
taboos: Monologue dump of the whole previous life
Foreknowledge claims that do not exist as prior_loop canon
judge_notes: Hindsight monologue at most 20% of the chapter (policy key rhythm.hindsight_monologue_max_ratio).
Every foreknowledge claim must map to a prior_loop fact; every deviation must be a canonical main-timeline event.
Satisfaction comes from pre-emption paying off on the page, not from the narrator asserting cleverness.

anchors.1: Recaps the first life instead of acting on it.
anchors.3: Acts on foreknowledge but explains it to the reader at length.
anchors.5: Foreknowledge shows in decisions and timing; recap is one italic line.

anchors.1: The future is fixed and nothing surprises the regressor.
anchors.5: A departure from the remembered future changes what the regressor can rely on, and the chapter makes the reader feel the ground move.

anchors.1: No payoff of the second-chance premise.
anchors.3: A payoff exists but is generic competence.
anchors.5: A specific first-life regret or threat is answered on the page.

calibration.notes: Starter profile (ADR-0043). Numeric values are starting points.
